verified_key_information_units.information: Key period-over-period changes included an 8% decline in served travelers (239 thousand in 2024 vs 259 thousand in 2023) and a swing from positive to negative EBITDA (€5.2m to -€6.1m). candidate_sentences.text: Novaturas Group’s audited 2024 revenue was EUR 200.9 million, down 3.6% from the restated 2023 figure of EUR 208.3 million, while passengers served decreased 7.6% to 239.5 thousand.

EBITDA declined from a positive EUR 5.2 million in 2023 to negative EUR 6.1 million, while adjusted EBITDA, excluding the goodwill impairment, fell from positive EUR 5.2 million to negative EUR 449 thousand.
The result included a one-off, non-cash goodwill impairment charge of EUR 5.7 million relating to the Estonian cash-generating unit; excluding this item, the net loss was EUR 1.9 million.

Management attributed the annual deterioration mainly to increased competition and oversupply of travel capacity in the Baltic States, which caused intense price competition, particularly in Turkey and the Greek islands.

verified_key_information_units.information: In early 2025, strategic investor Neset Kockar acquired 23.2% of Novaturas' shares (completed on 30 April 2025), with a planned further acquisition to reach 33.19% by autumn 2025. Kockar, a Turkish tourism businessman, provided the Group with loan facilities totaling EUR 2 million post-reporting-period, and is expected to bring synergies in destinations popular with Baltic travelers, potentially expanding hotel and travel offerings.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword; Note 29 (Events after the reporting period)

candidate_sentences.text: Management concluded that going concern remained appropriate, supported by planned operational improvements, expected 2025 EBITDA of EUR 2–3.3 million, new financing, and the post-year-end acquisition of a 23.2% stake by Turkish tourism investor Neset Kockar, who also provided EUR 2 million in loans.

verified_key_information_units.information: Travel demand trends showed significant growth to Spain (149% increase in passengers to Malaga, Barcelona, and Mallorca compared to 2022) and an 8% rise in long-haul travel. Popular long-haul destinations included Vietnam (+367%), Phuket (+23%), and Zanzibar (+21%), with long-haul flights achieving a 98.9% load factor in Q4 2024.

candidate_sentences.text: Growth in Spain, long-haul travel and group and workation trips also broadened demand.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operational performance improved materially in Q4 2024, with adjusted EBITDA reaching EUR 2.3 million and a load factor of 98.9% (compared to 96.7% in Q4 2023). This improvement followed optimization of the travel program and better destination management, reducing the share of last-minute trips which negatively impact financial results.

candidate_sentences.text: This contributed to a marked improvement in the latter part of the year: adjusted EBITDA was negative EUR 1.6 million in January–June but positive EUR 2.3 million in September–December.
Fourth-quarter load factor increased to 98.9% from 96.7%, and lower reliance on last-minute sales supported profitable fourth-quarter operations.

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity position weakened with cash and cash equivalents decreasing to EUR 394 thousand at 31 December 2024 from EUR 3,347 thousand in 2023. Borrowings increased to EUR 9,250 thousand (from EUR 8,682 thousand in 2023), and the Group did not comply with all financial covenants as of year-end, requiring waivers from lenders.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statements of cash flows; Note 14; Liquidity management section

candidate_sentences.text: Operating cash flow turned negative at EUR 1.6 million, compared with positive EUR 3.0 million in 2023, and cash fell to EUR 394 thousand from EUR 3.3 million.
Current liabilities exceeded current assets by EUR 12.5 million; the Group’s liquidity ratio declined to 0.51 from 0.65, while its debt-to-equity ratio rose to 121.1% from 58.0%.
The Group breached financing covenants at year-end but received waivers.

verified_key_information_units.information: Segment performance was dominated by flight packages, which accounted for the majority of revenue but saw a 12.3% decline in passenger numbers compared to 2023. Other segments included sightseeing tours by coach (3.7 thousand passengers) and by air (2.1 thousand), with 'other sales' (flight tickets and hotel bookings) growing by 12.8%.

candidate_sentences.text: Flight-package revenue, the Group’s main product, fell to EUR 170.7 million from EUR 182.8 million, partly offset by a 21.3% increase in other sales to EUR 25.4 million.
